intent: The single-line text field of a one-value combobox, showing the chosen item's label and taking the query that filters the list.
typical_uses: The field of a combobox that holds one value

dont_use_when.situation: A combobox that holds several values
A text field with no list of items to pick from

invariants.text: `className` and every forwarded attribute, including `aria-label`, `placeholder` and `aria-invalid`, land on the `<input>`, not on the span that wraps it and the trailing buttons.

With `showClear`, the clear button is in the DOM only while there is a chosen value, and while it is there combobox.module.css hides the trigger button, so the two never show at once; pressing it empties the field and the value.
The trigger and clear buttons take no keyboard focus (the primitive gives both `tabIndex` -1 while the field sits outside the popup); keyboard users open and operate the list from the field itself.
`disabled` disables the input and both trailing buttons together.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave the field with no accessible name
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible label; the placeholder is not a name

anti_patterns.dont: Keep the English default labels in a combobox shipped in another language
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `toggleLabel` and `clearLabel`; the trailing buttons are icon-only, so those strings are their only accessible names

a11y.by: the primitive gives the Combobox.Input element role="combobox"; combobox.test.tsx asserts the field is found by role combobox and name "Region", the trailing buttons by role button and the names "Toggle options" and "Clear value", and the overrides "Optionen umschalten" and "Auswahl löschen" when `toggleLabel` and `clearLabel` are passed

children.states: children is React content, rendered inside the wrapping span after the input and its trailing buttons, such as a ComboboxTrigger replacing the field's own
children.because: `ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the input's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the input's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, popupSide, listEmpty, readOnly, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside ComboboxInput behind `showClear`; the kit exports no clear button of its own.

good.title: A field with a clear button
good.code:
<Combobox items={regions}>
  <ComboboxInput aria-label="Region" placeholder="Pick a region" showClear />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>

good.title: Button names in another language
good.code:
<ComboboxInput
  aria-label="Region"
  showClear
  toggleLabel="Optionen umschalten"
  clearLabel="Auswahl löschen"
/>

bad.title: A trigger nested inside the field
bad.why: ComboboxInput already renders its own trigger button (`showTrigger` is on unless turned off), so this puts a second one in the same slot; drop the child, or pass `showTrigger={false}` so the child is the only one.

children.description: Partially typed: ReactNode. The compiler emits one JSON type per property and none for this one; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.partially_typed_props. children is React content, rendered inside the wrapping span after the input and its trailing buttons, such as a ComboboxTrigger replacing the field's own. `ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ComboboxInputState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the input's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the input's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, popupSide, listEmpty, readOnly, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.
